newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sluggish first-half sales hit Hyundai Motor, Kia.
newsitem.headline: Sluggish first-half sales hit Hyundai Motor, Kia.

text.p: The profitability of two major South Korean carmakers deteriorated in the first half from a year ago due largely to slumping domestic sales, company officials and analysts said.

South Korea's largest car maker Hyundai Motor Co said on Thursday its net profits in the first half had fallen to 28.16 billion won ($31.49 million) from 51.64 billion won a year earlier. Its sales declined to 5.42 trillion won from 5.56 trillion.
"Domestic sales were pretty slow in the first half because of the slowing economy," said a Hyundai spokesman.

Kia Motors Corp, one of the nation's three largest makers, said its losses widened to 37.0 billion won from a 10.34 billion loss a year ago, while its sales rose to 3.39 trillion won from 3.03 trillion.
Kia Motors is the flagship of eighth-ranked Kia Group, which was put under creditors' protection last month.
Officials and analysts said the debut of three new models by unlisted Daewoo Motor Co since last November also eroded sales of comparable models from Hyundai and Kia.
Daewoo's Lanos compact cars, which began selling late last year, took a big bite out of markets for Hyundai's Accent and Kia's Avella models.
Daewoo launched sales of its bigger Nubira compact cars in February and Leganza mid-sized sedans in April.
Analysts said Hyundai and Kia had to offer incentives to keep their market share, including non-interest installment sales, which cut deeply into their profit margins.
According to figures from the Korea Automobile Manufacturers Association, South Korean vehicle makers sold 724,883 vehicles at home in the first half, down from 817,275 units a year earlier.

Analysts said car sales may pick up in the second half in line with an expected economic recovery, but that competition would remain heated in the domestic market because of new models and sales incentives. (Conversion: $1 = 894.30 won)
